questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ takes the values 1, 2 and 3 and has cumulative distribution function $\mathrm{F}(x)$ given by

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 2 & 3\\ \hline \mathrm{F}(x) & 0.4 & 0.65 & 1\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: for $\mathrm{P}(X=1)=0.4$ and evidence of a correct method for finding $\mathrm{P}(X=2)$ or $\mathrm{P}(X=3)$. Implied by correct ans.
$\mathrm{P}(X=2)=\mathrm{F}(2)-\mathrm{F}(1)$ (o.e.)
1st A1: for $\mathrm{P}(X=2)=0.25$
2nd A1: for $\mathrm{P}(X=3)=0.35$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $x$: 1, 2, 3; $\mathrm{P}(X=x)$: $\underline{0.4}$, 0.25, 0.35

questions.stem: The time, in minutes, taken to fly from London to Malaga has a normal distribution with mean 150 minutes and standard deviation 10 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that the next flight from London to Malaga takes less than 145 minutes.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[\mathrm{P}(M<145)=]$ $\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{145-150}{10}\right)$ M1
$=\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.5)$ or $\mathrm{P}(Z>0.5)$ A1
$=$ awrt $0.309$ A1
Notes: M1 for standardising with 145, 150 and 10. Allow $\pm$ and use of symmetry so 155 instead of 145. 1st A1 for $\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.5)$ or $\mathrm{P}(Z>0.5)$ i.e. a $z$ value of $\pm 0.5$ and a correct region indicated. 2nd A1 for awrt 0.309. Answer only is 3/3.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone poor use of notation if a correct line appears later.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The time taken to fly from London to Berlin has a normal distribution with mean 100 minutes and standard deviation $d$ minutes.

Given that 15% of the flights from London to Berlin take longer than 115 minutes,

(b) find the value of the standard deviation $d$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $[\mathrm{P}(B>115)=0.15\Rightarrow]$ $\frac{115-100}{d}=1.0364$ M1B1A1
(Calc gives $1.036433...$)
$\underline{d=14.5}$ (Calc gives $14.4727...$) A1
Notes: M1 for $\pm\frac{115-100}{d}=z$ where $|z|>1$. Condone MR of $\mu=150$ instead of 100 for M1B1only. B1 for a standardised expression $=\pm 1.0364$ (do not allow for use of $1-1.0364$). 1st A1 for $z=$ awrt 1.04 and compatible signs i.e. a correct equation with $z=$ awrt 1.04. 2nd A1 for awrt 14.5 (allow awrt 14.4 if $z=$ awrt 1.04 is seen). Calc: Answer only of awrt 14.473 scores M1B1A1A1. Answer only of awrt 14.48 scores M1B0A1A1.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The time, $X$ minutes, taken to fly from London to another city has a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ minutes.

Given that $\mathrm{P}(X<\mu-15)=0.35$

(c) find $\mathrm{P}(X>\mu+15 \mid X>\mu-15)$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $[\mathrm{P}(X>\mu+15\mid X>\mu-15)=]$ $\frac{\mathrm{P}(X>\mu+15)}{\mathrm{P}(X>\mu-15)}$ M1
$=\frac{0.35}{1-0.35}$ A1
$=\frac{7}{13}$ or awrt $0.538$ A1
Notes: M1 for a correct ratio expression need $\mathrm{P}(X>\mu+15)$ on numerator. Allow use of a value for $\mu$. May be implied by next line. NB $\frac{0.35\times 0.65}{0.65}=\frac{0.2275}{0.65}$ is M0. 1st A1 for a correct ratio of probabilities. 2nd A1 for awrt 0.538 or $\frac{7}{13}$ (o.e.). Allow 0.5385 provided 2nd A1 is scored.

questions.stem:
The Venn diagram in Figure 1 shows three events $A$, $B$ and $C$ and the probabilities associated with each region of $B$. The constants $p$, $q$ and $r$ each represent probabilities associated with the three separate regions outside $B$.

The events $A$ and $B$ are independent.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[\mathrm{P}(B)=0.4, \mathrm{P}(A)=p+0.1$ so$]$ $0.4\times(p+0.1)=0.1$ or $0.4\times \mathrm{P}(A)=0.1$ M1
$p=\frac{1}{4}-0.1$ M1
$\underline{p=0.15}$ A1
Notes: 1st M1 for using independence in an attempt to form an equation in $p$ or $\mathrm{P}(A)$. 2nd M1 for a correct attempt to solve their linear equation leading to $p=...$. A1 for 0.15 or exact equivalent.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(B\mid C)=\frac{5}{11}$

(b) find the value of $q$ and the value of $r$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\frac{5}{11}=\left[\mathrm{P}(B\mid C)=\right]\frac{\mathrm{P}(B\cap C)}{\mathrm{P}(C)}=\frac{0.2}{0.2+q}$ or $\frac{5}{11}=\frac{0.2}{\mathrm{P}(C)}$ M1
$11\times 0.2=5\times(0.2+q)$ dM1
$\underline{q=0.24}$ A1
$r=0.6-(p+q)$ i.e. $\underline{r=0.21}$ A1ft
Notes: 1st M1 for a clear attempt to use $\mathrm{P}(B\mid C)$ to form an equation for $q$ or $\mathrm{P}(C)$. Assuming indep M0. 2nd dM1 Dep. on 1st M1 for correctly simplifying to a linear equation in $q$ or $\mathrm{P}(C)$ e.g. accept $11\times 0.2=5\times 0.2+q$ or $5\mathrm{P}(C)=2.2$. 1st A1 for $q=0.24$ or exact equivalent. 2nd A1ft for $0.6-$ their $(p+q)$ Dependent on 1st M1 in (b) only.

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\left[\frac{\mathrm{P}((A\cup C)\cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}\right]=\frac{0.3}{0.4}$ M1
$=\underline{0.75}$ A1
Notes: M1 for a correct ratio expression and one correct value (num < denom) or a fully correct ratio. Allow $\frac{\mathrm{P}(A\cup C\cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}$ with one probability correct but only if num < denom. A numerator of $\mathrm{P}(A\cup C)\times \mathrm{P}(B)$ scores M0. A1 for 0.75 or an exact equivalent.
